extracted.intended_audience: recipients of federal funds (school administrators, Title IX Coordinators), institutional legal counsel, and policymakers implementing Title IX grievance procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative and procedural standards for designing and operating Title IX grievance procedures (investigations, decisionmaking, appeals, and informal resolution) consistent with the Department's final regulations and accompanying interpretive guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on conflict of interest or bias for decisionmakers
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(b)(2): Prohibits any person from serving as a Title IX Coordinator, investigator, or decisionmaker if they have a conflict of interest or bias for or against complainants or respondents generally or an individual complainant or respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to all decisionmakers including those who decide appeals of dismissals; recipients retain discretion to determine bases for appeal other than those in §106.46(i). Determinations about conflicts are fact-specific; recipients may restrict job duties, train multiple employees for Title IX roles, hire outside personnel, or use designees to avoid conflicts. The Department declined to identify categorical role-based conflicts (e.g., principal, athletics director) because assignments vary by recipient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable treatment of complainants and respondents
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(b)(1): Requires a recipient to treat complainants and respondents equitably in its grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a foundational requirement informing all other procedural choices; recipients must ensure procedures and any differential application (e.g., single-investigator for some complaints) are explained and applied in a manner that treats parties equitably.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of respondent not responsible
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(b)(3): Grievance procedures must include a presumption that the respondent is not responsible for the alleged sex discrimination until a determination is made at the conclusion of the recipient's grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works together with evidence evaluation and decisionmaking standards to protect due process; part of the suite of safeguards against bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy protections
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(b)(5): Requires recipients to take reasonable steps to protect the privacy of the parties and witnesses during the grievance procedures (subject to certain exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Privacy protections are to be balanced with investigatory duties and disclosure obligations; used as one of the safeguards to support impartiality and trust in the grievance process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective evaluation of relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(b)(6) and §106.45(b)(7): Requires an objective evaluation of all relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence; definition of "relevant" per §106.2 applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes both inculpatory and exculpatory evidence. Decisionmakers must evaluate relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence for persuasiveness and must not find sex discrimination unless persuaded under the applicable standard of proof. Credibility determinations may not be based on a person's status as complainant, respondent, or witness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training for impartiality and neutrality
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.8(d): Requires recipients to train investigators (and other Title IX personnel) on how to serve impartially, including by avoiding prejudgment of the facts, conflicts of interest, and bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training is a specific safeguard the Department points to in maintaining integrity of investigations and decisionmaking; the Department references §106.8(d) elsewhere for detailed training requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal rights and standards
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(i) and §106.46(i): Recipients must offer parties an appeal that, at minimum, is the same as it offers in all other comparable proceedings, if any; §106.46(i) requires postsecondary institutions to offer an appeal based on factors that would change material aspects of the matter, including procedural irregularity that would change the outcome and decisionmaker conflict of interest or bias that would change the outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal decisionmakers must not have taken part in the investigation or dismissal of the complaint (§106.45(d)(3)(iii)); the Department declined to require live hearings for appeals but permits them at the recipient's discretion or when other law requires them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt and reasonable timeframes
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(b)(4) and §106.45(a)(1): Recipients must establish prompt and reasonable timeframes for their grievance procedures and have a broader duty to address complaints of sex discrimination in a 'prompt' manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must balance timeliness with fairness; the final regulations include protections against delay. The Department found permitting a single-investigator model can relieve administrative burden without sacrificing timeliness or quality, but recipients must still set and meet prompt timeframes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and handling of evidence gathered in investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(f)(3) and related provisions: In an investigation, the recipient must review all evidence gathered and determine what evidence is relevant and what evidence is impermissible regardless of relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must document the relevance determination; decisionmakers later evaluate the persuasiveness of that relevant evidence. This process is intended to prevent consideration of impermissible evidence and ensure both inculpatory and exculpatory information are considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-investigator model permitted with safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(b)(2) (final): The regulations permit, but do not require, a recipient to use a single-investigator model (investigator may also be decisionmaker and/or Title IX Coordinator) provided the person has no conflict of interest or bias and other protections in §106.45 are satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department emphasizes recipients' discretion to adopt the model to accommodate institutional circumstances. Concerns raised by commenters (impartiality, due process, resources, timeliness, risk of bias) must be addressed by the recipient through the anti-bias prohibitions, training, review safeguards, and appeal rights. Recipients may use multiple investigators, external investigators, panels, or require consent of parties if the institution chooses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance notice when single-investigator model will be used
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(b)(8): The Department added §106.45(b)(8) to require that a recipient's grievance procedures make the recipient's educational community aware in advance of when a recipient will utilize a single‑investigator model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a recipient uses different models for different complaints, the grievance procedures must articulate consistent principles for determining which procedures apply and must do so in a manner that treats complainants and respondents equitably.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent articulation of procedures when multiple models used
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(b)(8): If a recipient chooses to adopt grievance procedures that apply to the resolution of some but not all complaints (e.g., live hearing for some and single-investigator for others), the recipient must articulate consistent principles for how it will determine which procedures apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The determination regarding which model applies must treat complainants and respondents equitably and be explained in the recipient's published grievance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on informal resolution facilitator serving as investigator/decisionmaker
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.44(k)(4): The person who facilitates informal resolution cannot be the same person as the investigator or decisionmaker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This separation is intended to protect candor in informal resolution and prevent improper access, consideration, disclosure, or other use of information obtained solely through informal resolution if the matter proceeds to grievance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation to designees (including nonemployees) permitted with compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.8(a)(2): A recipient may delegate duties under the final regulations to designees, including designees who are not employees of the recipient, provided implementation of grievance procedures satisfies all requirements of the final regulations, including training designees consistent with §106.8(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may use external investigators or adjudicators to avoid conflicts or manage resources, but must ensure such designees are trained and that their use complies with all procedural safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credibility assessment procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of §106.45(g) and related sections: Recipients must provide a process that enables the decisionmaker to question parties and witnesses to adequately assess credibility, to the extent credibility is both in dispute and relevant to evaluating allegations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department rejects the view that single-investigator models inherently inhibit credibility testing. Requirements include objective evaluation of all relevant evidence and prohibition on basing credibility on status; recipients must still provide mechanisms (e.g., questioning procedures) sufficient to assess persuasiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisionmaker independence for appeals and dismissals
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(d)(3)(iii) and related discussion: The decisionmaker for an appeal must not have taken part in the investigation of the allegations or the dismissal of the complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This specific independence requirement is one safeguard ensuring that appeals address concerns about bias or procedural irregularities in the initial process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility to structure grievance procedures consistent with Title IX
rubrics_metrics.description: Throughout discussion: Recipients have discretion to choose models (single investigator, multiple investigators, internal/external personnel, panels) as long as the grievance procedures meet the final regulations' requirements and treat parties equitably.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department stressed flexibility to accommodate institutional size, resources, administrative structures, educational communities, and applicable State law, while maintaining required safeguards (anti-bias rules, training, evidence evaluation, appeals, timeliness, and transparency about models used).
